title: A WeChat-delivered Information-Motivation-Behavioral skills intervention to improve HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《A WeChat-delivered Information-Motivation-Behavioral skills intervention to improve HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p6】The present study addressed this gap by conducting a randomized controlled trial to test a culturally adapted intervention grounded in the IMB model and delivered via WeChat. We evaluated whether this approach could enhance HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese MSM, providing timely insights in the context of China’s evolving HPV vaccination policy.

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and a leading cause of anal, penile, and oropharyngeal cancers, particularly among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (MSM).1,2 In China, sexual minority men bear a disproportionate burden, with anal HPV prevalence ranging from 53.6% among HIV-negative individuals to 85.1% among those living with HIV.3,4 Regional studies from Urumqi and Shenzhen report anal HPV prevalence exceeding 51.8% among HIV-negative MSM and 70.0% among HIV-positive MSM.5,6 Moreover, HIV co-infection is associated with an increased risk of high-risk HPV infection and subsequent HPV-related cancers.4,6

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《A WeChat-delivered Information-Motivation-Behavioral skills intervention to improve HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and participants · s0002-s2001-p1】The study employed a parallel-group randomized controlled trial. Eligible participants were males aged 18–45 y who self-identified as gay or bisexual, or who reported having sex with men; were residents of China; had not received any HPV vaccination; and were active WeChat users. The exclusion criteria were unwillingness to provide follow-up information, prior participation in pilot HPV vaccination studies, and inability to read or access WeChat-delivered content. The full CONSORT 2025 checklist is provided in Table S4.

【Study design and participants · s0002-s2001-p2】A total of 684 participants provided informed consent and completed the baseline questionnaire. Participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the intervention group (n = 351) or the control group (n = 333). The intervention group received a 5-d HPV Vaccine Promotion Program (HPVVP), which delivered 12 multimedia messages focused on HPV and HPV vaccination among MSM. Content included short videos, infographics, and concise text summaries, with one to three messages delivered daily. Minimal reference was made to HIV. Participants could also submit HPV-related questions through the HPVVP consultation page. The control group received time-matched HIV-related multimedia health messages developed by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Outcomes were assessed at three time points: baseline (T0), immediately post-intervention (T1), and 1 month post-intervention (T2).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《A WeChat-delivered Information-Motivation-Behavioral skills intervention to improve HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · s0006-p1】In this randomized controlled trial, a brief IMB-guided intervention delivered via a WeChat official account improved short-term HPV vaccine acceptability among unvaccinated adult men in mainland China who self-identified as gay or bisexual, including those reporting sex with men. The intervention’s effects were consistent with IMB theory, operating primarily through strengthening key, modifiable determinants of acceptability – information, social motivation, and behavioral skills – although benefits diminished over time, underscoring the need for reinforcement and implementation support. In the context of China’s expanding access to male HPV vaccination, WeChat-based programs may offer a scalable, privacy-preserving approach to increasing readiness for vaccination among sexual minority men defined by identity or behavior. However, sustained public health impact will likely require booster engagement and linkage to stigma-sensitive, accessible services that address persistent structural barriers.

【Intervention development · s0002-s2005-p2】Development of the HPVVP intervention followed an iterative process guided by an expert panel comprising three epidemiologists from the Jiangsu CDC, one physician specializing in MSM health education, three NGO representatives with experience in HIV service delivery, and one academic expert in social media – based interventions. Weekly meetings were held to ensure content accuracy, user engagement, cultural appropriateness, and usability. Intervention modules were refined through repeated review and testing, drawing on World Health Organization recommendations, published literature, Chinese CDC guidelines, and United Kingdom National Health Service standards. Figure 1 and Table 1 summarize the intervention flow, content, alignment with the IMB model, and delivery schedule. The names of panel members are listed in Table S5; for privacy protection, pseudonyms were used for some experts.
